segments.source: Problem 371. Pairwise collective choice: Park versus Library
Group preferences can be aggregated in different ways. Pairwise majority asks a specific question about two options at a time.

Three public projects are considered: Park, Library, Sports Hall. Voter groups and rankings: 4 voters rank Park>Library>Sports Hall; 5 voters rank Library>Sports Hall>Park; 2 voters rank Sports Hall>Park>Library. Use pairwise majority: compare two options at a time; each voter supports the one ranked higher.
For a pairwise contest, count how many voters prefer each of the two options. Ignore the third option for that comparison.
In a pairwise vote between Park and Library, which option wins?
1. For each group, check whether Park or Library is ranked higher. 2. Totals: Park=6, Library=5. 3. Therefore the result is Park.
A collective decision rule must be explicit; different rules can summarize the same rankings differently.
Preference rankings; for pair (a,b), sum weights of voters ranking a>b versus b>a.
